info.title: Queue OpenAPI for fal-ai/smart-resize
info.description: The OpenAPI schema for the fal-ai/smart-resize queue.

x-fal-metadata.about:
Resize an image to one or more exact target dimensions. Smart Resize
uses nano-banana-pro internally: for each requested ``<width>x<height>``
the endpoint
picks the smallest nano-banana-pro preset that fully covers the
target, regenerates the image with an adaptive prompt, and then
center-crops it to the exact requested dimensions so the output is
pixel-perfect.

seed.title: Seed
seed.description: Optional random seed forwarded to the inner nano-banana-pro /edit calls for reproducibility. The same seed is used for every target size when set.

resolution.title: Resolution
resolution.description: Hint for the minimum resolution tier to use internally. The smart-resize algorithm may pick a higher tier automatically when the requested target size is too large for this tier. This field does not affect the final output dimensions — those come from ``target_sizes``.

image_url.title: Image URL
image_url.description: The URL of the source image to resize.

target_sizes.title: Target Sizes
target_sizes.description: The list of target dimensions to generate, each written as ``<width>x<height>`` (e.g. ``"1920x1080"``). One output image is produced per target size (multiplied by ``num_images_per_size``). The endpoint internally picks the smallest nano-banana-pro preset that fully covers each target so the final image is a pixel-perfect match with no upscaling.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.description: Optional extra instruction that is forwarded to nano-banana-pro alongside the auto-generated resize prompt. Leave empty to let the model preserve the original image content as closely as possible.

sync_mode.title: Sync Mode
sync_mode.description: When True, the response contains data URIs in place of CDN URLs so the client can decode the images without an extra HTTP request. Adds latency for large outputs.

num_images_per_size.title: Num Images Per Size
num_images_per_size.description: The number of nano-banana-pro variants to produce for each target size. The response images list will contain ``len(target_sizes) * num_images_per_size`` images in total.

safety_tolerance.title: Safety Tolerance
safety_tolerance.description: The safety tolerance level applied to the inner nano-banana-pro /edit calls. Higher numbers loosen safety filtering.

results.title: Results
results.description: Per-target-size breakdown with the requested width/height and the nano-banana-pro (aspect_ratio, resolution) preset that was used internally.

description.title: Description
description.description: The description of the generated images.

images.title: Images
images.description: All generated images, flattened across every target size. Order matches the order of ``results`` below: the first ``num_images_per_size`` entries correspond to ``target_sizes[0]`` and so on.

SmartResizeResult.title: SmartResizeResult
SmartResizeResult.description:
Per-target-size resize result: a list of ``ImageFile`` objects all at the
exact requested (width, height).

resolution.title: Resolution
resolution.description: The nano-banana-pro resolution tier that was used internally for this target size.

description.title: Description
description.description: The description of the generated images.

height.title: Height
height.description: The requested target height in pixels.

aspect_ratio.title: Aspect Ratio
aspect_ratio.description: The nano-banana-pro aspect ratio that was used internally for this target size.

width.title: Width
width.description: The requested target width in pixels.

url.title: Url
url.description: The URL where the file can be downloaded from.

content_type.title: Content Type
content_type.description: The mime type of the file.

file_size.title: File Size
file_size.description: The size of the file in bytes.

file_name.title: File Name
file_name.description: The name of the file. It will be auto-generated if not provided.

schema.description: Whether to include logs (`1`) in the response or not (`0`).

success.description: Whether the request was cancelled successfully.
